- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, especially if recent prices are falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after strong upward sentiment spikes; apply a 5–10% downward correction to forecast peak values.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a lagged correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for each day of sentiment decay.
- Mean reversion is evident when forecast deviates >15% from 30-day moving average; bring forecast back toward historical mean, especially if sentiment is neutral or weak.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; dampen volatility by smoothing with 7-day moving average if sentiment is erratic.
